title: Spectral Perturbation Bounds for Low-Rank Approximation with Applications to Privacy

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text cites '[48, 49]' ('further refined in [48, 49]'), '[50]' ('first observed in the unpublished manuscript [50]'), and '[47]' ('the recent survey [47]'), but the reference list contains exactly entries [1]-[46]. Four in-text citations point to nonexistent references, including one used to attribute the provenance of the paper's central contour-bootstrapping technique.

Lemma 3.1 states the gap condition 'delta_p > 5||E||' and claims this 'strengthened gap condition is necessary'. Its own proof assumes '4||E|| < delta_p' and derives min|z-lambda_i| >= delta_p/2 >= 2||E||, which is exactly what closes the bootstrap; no 5||E|| condition is used anywhere. Theorems 2.1-2.3 all invoke the lemma under 4||E|| <= delta_p, so as printed the lemma cannot support the theorems that cite it.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract vs Appendix C Table 2 and Section 4
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Abstract claims 'near-perfect tracking of the actual spectral error under all tested perturbation regimes' and that the bounds are 'essentially tight in practice'. The paper's own Table 2 (Appendix C) reports 'our bound/true error' ratios of 87.02-90.17 at every tested noise level (an ~90x overestimate), and Section 4 concedes trials where the bound exceeded the error by more than 10x.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4 (Setting vs gap check vs Results)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Adult dataset dimension is stated as n=14 in the Setting, n=6 in the gap-condition check ('For Adult (n=6, p=4) ... 8*sqrt(6) ~ 19.6'; with n=14 the threshold would be 8*sqrt(14) ~ 29.93), and '6x6' in the Results. Additionally, a 'synthetic high-dimensional matrix (n=1200)' is introduced in the Setting but never appears in any reported result.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5 Conclusion and Section 2 vs Appendix C
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Conclusion claims 'strictly tighter guarantees in all practical regimes' (superseding Eckart-Young-Mirsky), and Section 2 claims the bound 'strictly dominates the Frobenius norm bounds of [29, 30] in all parameter regimes'. The paper's own Appendix C states 'our bound outperforms the classical bound precisely when 4||E|| < delta_p', with Table 2 showing the classical bound tighter (ratio > 1) for ||E||/delta_p >= 0.30.

The claim '||U_p U_p^T - Utilde_p Utilde_p^T|| = O~(||E||/lambda_p + 1/delta_p) [33, 37]' is dimensionally impossible: the projector difference is scale-invariant while 1/delta_p has units of inverse eigenvalue (rescaling (A,E) -> (cA,cE) changes the RHS but not the LHS). Standard Davis-Kahan-type results give O(||E||/delta_p).

'After applying our novel spectral regularization preprocessing (which adds 0.1*lambda_1*I to the covariance matrix), the gap condition 4||E_k|| < delta_p holds robustly'. Adding c*I shifts every eigenvalue by exactly c and leaves every eigengap delta_p = lambda_p - lambda_{p+1} unchanged, so this operation cannot affect the gap condition.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix D.1, proof of Theorem D.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: 'Since p < n, then k+1 > n-(p-k)+1' is provably reversed: k+1 > n-(p-k)+1 is equivalent to p > n, contradicting p < n. The correct statement is k+1 <= n-(p-k), which is what actually implies k+1 lies outside the selected top-p index set.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2 and Section 4 (citation [41] for Wigner norm concentration)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: '||E|| = (2+o(1))sqrt(n) with high probability [41, 43]' cites [41] = Van Huffel & Vandewalle, 'On the accuracy of total least squares...', Automatica 25(5):765-769 (1989) — verified via web search to be a simulation study of total least squares regression with no result on spectral norms of random matrices. The paper itself cites the correct pair [40, 43] (van Handel; Vu) for the identical claim in Corollary 2.4, indicating [41] is a wrong-reference substitution for [40].

'We exclude 12 outlier trials (1.3%)': the declared design is 3 datasets x 2 noise models x 20 noise levels x 100 trials = 12,000 trials, so 12 trials = 0.1%; 1.3% would imply ~923 total trials, matching no stated configuration. The same paragraph also claims the estimate 'never deviates from the observed error by more than a single order of magnitude' while the exclusion criterion concedes deviations exceeding 10x occurred.

'alpha chosen over 11 evenly spaced values such that ||E||/delta_p in {0.05, 0.10, ..., 0.50}': the enumerated set contains exactly 10 values (step 0.05 from 0.05 to 0.50), and Table 2 reports exactly 10 columns. 11 != 10.

The proof asserts '(zI-A)^{-1} - (zI-Atilde)^{-1} = (zI-A)^{-1} E (zI-Atilde)^{-1}'. The stated identity M^{-1}-(M+N)^{-1}=(M+N)^{-1}NM^{-1} with M=zI-Atilde, N=E gives (zI-Atilde)^{-1}-(zI-A)^{-1} = (zI-A)^{-1}E(zI-Atilde)^{-1}; the printed left-hand side is reversed (a sign error). Downstream steps survive only because norms are taken.

The pipeline claims 'each column is centered and whitened' before computing 'the covariance matrix A := M^T M'. Whitened columns yield a covariance proportional to the identity, making all eigenvalues nearly equal (delta_p ~ 0) — directly contradicting the reported gaps (delta_p ~ 1433.99 for Census, 351.3 for KDD) on which the gap-condition validation rests. The paragraph also excludes 'MNIST, CIFAR-10, ImageNet', datasets never part of the stated setup.

The Introduction attributes the open question to '[29, Remark 5.3] and [30, Section 6.2]' and the Contributions claim to resolve '[29, Remark 5.3]', but Corollary 2.4's discussion claims to be 'resolving the open question posed in [30, Remark 5.3]' — attributing 'Remark 5.3' to a different paper than the rest of the text.

[44] and [45] are the same Wainwright book ('High-dimensional statistics: A non-asymptotic viewpoint', vol. 48, Cambridge University Press, 2019) listed twice under different numbers, and both numbers are cited in the text.

Theorem 2.1 adds 'The strict inequality is essential for the contour construction in the proof; the case 4||E|| = delta_p requires separate analysis.' This is false by the paper's own argument: with 4||E|| = delta_p the key estimate min|z-lambda_i| >= delta_p/2 >= 2||E|| still holds, giving the same F <= 2F_1 bootstrap. Theorems 2.2 and 2.3 state the identical condition non-strictly.

Column contents do not match headers (guarantee types under 'Norm', norms under 'Noise model', noise models under 'Assumption'), and the EYM bound is labeled 'High-probability' although the paper itself (Section 1, Appendix G) describes it as a deterministic bound holding for arbitrary matrices and noise.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix D.2, combination of Eqs (7)-(8) into the final bound
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Equations (7) and (8) contain log(10*sigma_1/delta) terms, whose sum is log(100*sigma_1^2/(delta_k*delta_{n-(p-k)})); the final display instead writes log(36*sigma_1^2/(...)), a strictly smaller quantity that does not follow from (7)+(8). The constant chain (7),(8) -> final display -> Theorem D.5 statement is internally inconsistent.

summary: Exhaustive strict-mode verification of this spectral perturbation theory paper found 17 errors, many at high confidence. The core theory has internal consistency failures: Lemma 3.1 states a gap condition (delta_p > 5||E||) contradicted by its own proof and by the theorems that invoke it under 4||E|| <= delta_p; Theorem 2.1 falsely claims strict inequality is 'essential'; the resolvent identity in Lemma 3.1's proof has a sign error; a proof step in Appendix D.1 asserts an inequality equivalent to p > n under the hypothesis p < n; Appendix D.2's constant chain is inconsistent (log 36 vs log 100); and Appendix B displays a dimensionally impossible projector bound (O~(||E||/lambda_p + 1/delta_p)). The empirical section is internally contradictory: the Adult dataset is n=14, n=6, and 6x6 in the same section; a promised n=1200 synthetic experiment never appears; the preprocessing pipeline (column whitening) would destroy the very eigengaps it reports; a claimed spectral regularization (adding 0.1*lambda_1*I) cannot affect eigengaps; outlier accounting (12 trials = 1.3%) is arithmetically impossible under the stated 12,000-trial design; and Appendix C claims 11 noise levels for a 10-value set and 10-column table. Citation integrity is compromised: four in-text citations ([47]-[50]) point to nonexistent references, [41] (a total-least-squares paper, verified externally) is cited for Wigner-matrix norm concentration in place of [40], the open question's source flips between [29] and [30], and [44]/[45] duplicate the same book. At the macro level, the Abstract's claims of 'near-perfect tracking' and practical tightness 'under all tested perturbation regimes' are contradicted by the paper's own Table 2 (bound/true-error ratios of 87-90), and the Conclusion's 'strictly tighter guarantees in all practical regimes' is contradicted by Appendix C, which shows the classical EYM bound is tighter for ||E||/delta_p >= 0.30. The underlying contour-bootstrapping mathematics is largely sound, but the paper requires substantial correction before its statements, experiments, citations, and claims are mutually consistent.
